newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish sharemarket climbs to new all-time high.
newsitem.headline: Swedish sharemarket climbs to new all-time high.

text.p: The Stockholm bourse closed at a record high on Monday after blue-chip Ericsson made handsome gains with brokers expecting more increases across the board.
The bourse's general index closed at 2,016.84, up 0.83 percent, toppling a record of 2,000.21 set on Friday. Brokers said the index could easily be broken again on Tuesday.

"We find ourselves in the best of all possible worlds with a positive scenario for the business cycle and no large rate increases expected in the U.S.," one broker said. "I believe we can see a couple positive weeks ahead of us for the market."
Turnover was slight above average at 3.5 billion crowns.
"After the latest upturn, there was noone who dared dig their heels in completely. That's why the turnover and the upturn was not exceptionally large," one broker said.
A large part of the gains were owed to a jump by telecoms group Ericsson, which closed up 4.50 crowns at 163 after rising in New York on Friday.
Drug company Astra edged up one crown to 279.50.
Steel shares rose, with SSAB closing at 100 crowns, up 2.50, and Avesta Sheffield rising two crowns to 71.
The forestry sector index fell 0.24 percent.
